concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Fractions
concepts.key_idea: A fraction represents part of a whole using a numerator and denominator.
concepts.teacher_note: Use familiar objects such as roti, fruit, chocolate bars, or fraction strips.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Percentage
concepts.key_idea: Percentage means a value out of 100 and is calculated as part divided by whole multiplied by 100.
concepts.teacher_note: Watch for students reversing obtained marks and total marks.

concepts.subject: Science
concepts.name: Physical and Chemical Changes
concepts.key_idea: A physical change does not form a new substance; a chemical change forms a new substance.
concepts.teacher_note: Use melting ice and burning paper to separate reversible clues from the stronger new-substance test.

concepts.subject: Science
concepts.name: Photosynthesis
concepts.key_idea: Green plants make food from carbon dioxide and water using sunlight and chlorophyll.
concepts.teacher_note: Frame the leaf as a food factory to make inputs and outputs concrete.

concepts.subject: Hindi
concepts.name: Sandhi
concepts.key_idea: Sandhi is the change that happens when two sounds or letters combine.
concepts.teacher_note: Teach Sandhi and Sandhi-vichhed together with simple word splitting.

concepts.subject: Hindi
concepts.name: Samas
concepts.key_idea: Samas combines two or more words into a shorter compound word.
concepts.teacher_note: Contrast Samas with Sandhi so students see word compression versus sound change.

concepts.subject: English
concepts.name: Tenses
concepts.key_idea: Tense tells the time of an action: present, past, or future.
concepts.teacher_note: Use time clues such as today, yesterday, and tomorrow.

concepts.subject: English
concepts.name: Subject-Verb Agreement
concepts.key_idea: The subject and verb must agree in number and person.
concepts.teacher_note: Focus on simple-present third-person singular examples.

questions.easy_explanation: If the numerator is the same, the smaller denominator gives the bigger piece.
questions.common_mistake: Thinking that the bigger denominator means the bigger fraction.
questions.reteach_method: Show the same roti divided into halves and quarters, then compare one piece from each.

questions.question_text: What is a fraction? Explain numerator and denominator using 3/5.
questions.correct_answer: A fraction is part of a whole. In 3/5, 3 is the numerator and 5 is the denominator.
questions.easy_explanation: Imagine 5 equal pieces of chocolate. If 3 are taken, the fraction is 3/5.
questions.common_mistake: Mixing up the numerator and denominator.
questions.reteach_method: Ask the learner to draw 5 boxes and shade 3 of them.

questions.question_text: A student scored 45 marks out of 60. Find the percentage.
questions.easy_explanation: Percentage means out of 100: 45 divided by 60 multiplied by 100 is 75.
questions.common_mistake: Dividing total marks by obtained marks.
questions.reteach_method: Write part divided by whole multiplied by 100, then identify part and whole from the question.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a physical change and a chemical change? Give one example of each.
questions.correct_answer: A physical change forms no new substance, such as melting ice. A chemical change forms a new substance, such as burning paper.
questions.easy_explanation: Ice melting is still water. Paper burning creates ash and gases.
questions.common_mistake: Using reversibility as the only test.
questions.reteach_method: Sort classroom examples into 'new substance formed' and 'no new substance formed'.

questions.question_text: What do plants need for photosynthesis?
questions.correct_answer: Carbon dioxide, water, sunlight, and chlorophyll.
questions.easy_explanation: A green leaf uses sunlight like energy to make food from water and carbon dioxide.
questions.reteach_method: Draw a leaf and label inputs, helper, food output, and oxygen output.

questions.question_text: Sandhi kya hai? Him + aalay ka sandhi roop likhiye.
questions.correct_answer: Do varnon ke mel se hone wale parivartan ko sandhi kahte hain. Him + aalay = Himalaya.
questions.easy_explanation: Jab do sounds milkar shabd ka roop badalte hain, use sandhi kahte hain.
questions.reteach_method: Pehle mool sounds dikhayein, phir naya shabd bolkar aur likhkar tulna karvayein.

questions.question_text: Samas kya hai? Raja ka putra ka samast pad likhiye.
questions.correct_answer: Do ya adhik shabdon ko milakar sankshipt naya shabd banana samas hai. Raja ka putra = rajputra.
questions.easy_explanation: Lambe word group ko chhota karke naya word banana samas hai.
questions.common_mistake: Samas-vigrah aur samast pad ko ulta likhna.
questions.reteach_method: Ek taraf vistaar roop aur doosri taraf sankshipt roop likhvayein.

questions.question_text: Correct this sentence: I go to school yesterday.
questions.easy_explanation: Yesterday tells us the action happened in the past, so use went.
questions.common_mistake: Using present tense with a past-time word.
questions.reteach_method: Make a three-column chart: today I go, yesterday I went, tomorrow I will go.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct sentence: She play cricket. / She plays cricket.
questions.easy_explanation: In simple present tense, she usually takes a verb ending in s or es.
questions.common_mistake: Forgetting the s with he, she, or it.
questions.reteach_method: Compare I play, they play, and she plays with spoken examples.
